p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines the *never-escalate* law for integrations that act under a credential: *what* it means for an integration to stay inside its declared scope, *how* an explicit prefix check enforces it, *why* an escalation is an error rather than a warning, how *trust ordering* between sources keeps a lower-trust answer from overriding a higher-trust one, and *why* these rules live globally rather than per-module.

p.sibling-document-pointers: It is the companion to the four laws in [`SECRETS-HYGIENE-PROTOCOL.md`](SECRETS-HYGIENE-PROTOCOL.md).

p.AN-INTEGRATION-IS-BOUND-TO-ITS-GRANTED-S: An integration that operates on behalf of a credential is bound to the **scope that credential was granted for**, and must refuse to touch anything outside it.

p.act-on-the-declared-target-and-nowhere-e: If the project declares that publishing targets organization `X` on some host, the integration that creates, updates, or even *probes* repositories may act on `X` and nowhere else:

facts.SCOPE-NO-OTHER-ORGANIZATIONS: **No other organizations** on the same host.
facts.SCOPE-NO-USER-NAMESPACES: **No user namespaces** on the same host.
facts.SCOPE-NO-UNRELATED-ENDPOINTS: **No endpoints** unrelated to the target — no account-wide reads, no listing of resources outside `X`.

p.a-credential-may-technically-reach-furth: The credential may technically be able to reach further — a token scoped broadly can write to many repos.

p.THE-DECLARED-SCOPE-IS-THE-BOUNDARY: The declared scope is the boundary, and the integration enforces it even when the credential would allow more.

prefix-checks.title: Explicit prefix checks

p.THE-LAW-IS-ENFORCED-BY-AN-EXPLICIT-CHECK: The law is enforced by an **explicit check in the adapter**, not by convention or by hoping the target is right.

p.prefix-comparison-lead: Before an integration acts, it computes the target's owning scope and compares it against the declared scope by prefix:

prefix-checks.fence:
target = "host.example/acme-org/some-repo" declared_scope = "host.example/acme-org"
if not target.starts_with(declared_scope + "/"): raise ScopeError(target, declared_scope) # refuse, do not warn

p.THE-CHECK-IS-A-GUARD-AT-THE-BOUNDARY: The check is a **guard at the boundary** — the single point where the integration is about to act on a resource.

p.AN-UNGUARDED-CODE-PATH-IS-A-BUG: A code path that reaches a host endpoint without passing the check is a bug, caught in review, on the same footing as a code path that prints a secret value.

error-not-warning.title: Escalation is an error, not a warning

p.A-FAILED-CHECK-RAISES-AN-ERROR-AND-REFUS: When the prefix check fails, the integration **raises an error and refuses the action**.

p.IT-DOES-NOT-WARN-AND-PROCEED: It does not log a warning and proceed; it does not act "just this once" against an out-of-scope target.

p.THERE-IS-NO-RUNTIME-OVERRIDE-FLAG: There is no override flag that quietly widens the boundary at runtime.

p.the-reason-is-the-blast-radius: The reason is the blast radius.

p.a-warning-is-indistinguishable-from-succ: A warning that scrolls past in a log is indistinguishable from success to an automated run — and an out-of-scope write has already happened by the time anyone reads the warning.

p.AN-ERROR-STOPS-BEFORE-THE-BOUNDARY-IS-CR: An error stops the action *before* the boundary is crossed, which is the only point where stopping is still cheap.

p.WIDENING-SCOPE-IS-AN-OWNER-CONFIGURATION: Widening the scope is a deliberate configuration change to the declared scope, made by the owner, reviewed like any other change — never a runtime decision made by the adapter under pressure.

p.SCOPE-DISCIPLINE-EXTENDS-TO-READING: Scope discipline extends to *reading*, not only writing.

p.trust-order-highest-first-lead: When the same question can be answered by several sources of differing trust — a primary registry and a mirror, a canonical index and a fallback — the sources are consulted in **trust order**, highest first, and the first source with a valid answer **wins outright**:

facts.TRUST-ITERATE-IN-PRIORITY-ORDER: The resolver iterates sources in priority order.
facts.TRUST-FIRST-VALID-ANSWER-TERMINATES: The first that returns a satisfying answer terminates the search.
facts.TRUST-ANSWERS-ARE-NOT-MERGED: Answers are **not merged** across sources of different trust.

p.this-prevents-a-lower-trust-source-from-: This prevents a lower-trust source from influencing a result when a higher-trust source already has a valid answer.

p.unioning-would-let-a-malicious-mirror-in: If answers were unioned, a compromised or malicious low-trust mirror could inject an entry — a poisoned version, a redirect to an attacker's artifact — into a resolution that a trusted source had already settled.

p.TRUST-ORDERING-CLOSES-THAT-SURFACE: Trust ordering closes that: once the trusted source answers, the untrusted one is never consulted for that question, so it has no surface to influence.

tr.td: What a malicious low-trust source can do

td.fact: Inject an entry into any resolution — a poisoned version wins if it sorts first
Nothing, once a trusted source has answered — it is never consulted

p.SCOPE-DISCIPLINE-IS-A-GLOBAL-INVARIANT: Like the four laws, scope discipline is a **global invariant**, not a per-module convention.

p.the-reason-is-again-blast-radius: The reason is again blast radius: an escalated integration is not a bounded, local failure — it is the **whole host account**, every resource the credential can reach.

p.one-forgotten-check-is-enough-to-realize: A single adapter that forgot its prefix check, or a single resolver path that merged an untrusted source, is enough to realize that failure.

p.a-catastrophic-rule-cannot-live-per-modu: A rule that must hold on *every* path, whose violation on *any* path is catastrophic, cannot live in each module's local discipline and be trusted to have been reimplemented correctly everywhere.

p.IT-LIVES-ONCE-GLOBALLY-AND-EVERY-PATH-IS: It lives once, globally, and every code path that acts under a credential or resolves across trust boundaries is audited against it.

p.module-local-rules-bound-module-local-bl: Module-local rules bound module-local blast; these failures are not module-local.

facts.SUM-ACT-ONLY-INSIDE-THE-DECLARED-SCOPE: An integration acts only inside the scope its credential was declared for — no other orgs, no user namespaces, no unrelated endpoints. Technical reach is not permission.
facts.SUM-ENFORCEMENT-IS-AN-EXPLICIT-PREFIX-CH: Enforcement is an explicit prefix check at the boundary, run on every action.
facts.SUM-A-VIOLATION-IS-AN-ERROR-NOT-A-WARNIN: A scope violation is an **error that refuses the action**, never a warning that proceeds. Widening scope is an owner configuration change, not a runtime decision.
facts.SUM-TRUST-ORDERING-HIGHEST-FIRST-NEVER-M: Trust ordering: consult sources highest-trust first, first valid answer wins, never merge — so a low-trust source cannot influence a resolution a trusted source has settled.
facts.SUM-GLOBAL-BECAUSE-THE-BLAST-RADIUS-IS-T: These rules are global because the blast radius is the whole account; every credential-bearing path is audited against them.
